Let the position vectors of \(B\) and \(C\) relative to \(A\) be \(\mathbf b\) and \(\mathbf c\), with
\[
|\mathbf b|=11,\qquad |\mathbf c|=13.
\]
Write \(s=\mathbf b\cdot \mathbf c\). The centroid is
\[
\mathbf G=\frac{\mathbf b+\mathbf c}{3}.
\]
Since \(O\) is the circumcenter, equating distances from \(O\) to \(A,B,C\) gives
\[
\mathbf O\cdot\mathbf b=\frac{|\mathbf b|^2}{2}=\frac{121}{2},\qquad
\mathbf O\cdot\mathbf c=\frac{|\mathbf c|^2}{2}=\frac{169}{2}.
\]

Let \(\mathbf H\) be the orthocenter of \(\triangle AGO\). Since \(\mathbf H\) lies on line \(BC\),
\[
\mathbf H=\lambda\mathbf b+\mu\mathbf c,\qquad \lambda+\mu=1.
\]
The altitude conditions for the orthocenter of \(\triangle AGO\) imply
\[
\mathbf H\cdot\mathbf G=\mathbf G\cdot\mathbf O
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathbf H\cdot\mathbf O=\mathbf G\cdot\mathbf O.
\]

Compute
\[
\mathbf G\cdot\mathbf O
=\left(\frac{\mathbf b+\mathbf c}{3}\right)\cdot\mathbf O
=\frac{1}{3}(\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf O+\mathbf c\cdot\mathbf O)
=\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{121}{2}+\frac{169}{2}\right)
=\frac{145}{3}.
\]
Also,
\[
\mathbf H\cdot\mathbf O
=(\lambda\mathbf b+\mu\mathbf c)\cdot\mathbf O
=\lambda\cdot\frac{121}{2}+\mu\cdot\frac{169}{2}
=\frac{121\lambda+169\mu}{2}.
\]
Since \(\mathbf H\cdot\mathbf O=\mathbf G\cdot\mathbf O\),
\[
\frac{121\lambda+169\mu}{2}=\frac{145}{3}
\]
so
\[
121\lambda+169\mu=\frac{290}{3}.
\]

Now compute
\[
\mathbf H\cdot\mathbf G
=\left(\frac{\mathbf b+\mathbf c}{3}\right)\cdot(\lambda\mathbf b+\mu\mathbf c)
=\frac{1}{3}\bigl[\lambda(121+s)+\mu(s+169)\bigr].
\]
Since \(\mathbf H\cdot\mathbf G=\mathbf G\cdot\mathbf O=145/3\),
\[
\lambda(121+s)+\mu(s+169)=145.
\]
Using \(\lambda+\mu=1\),
\[
121\lambda+169\mu+s=145.
\]
But \(121\lambda+169\mu=290/3\), so
\[
s=145-\frac{290}{3}=\frac{145}{3}.
\]

Finally,
\[
BC^2=|\mathbf b-\mathbf c|^2
=|\mathbf b|^2+|\mathbf c|^2-2\,\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf c
=121+169-2\cdot\frac{145}{3}
=290-\frac{290}{3}
=\frac{580}{3}.
\]
Therefore
\[
BC=\sqrt{\frac{580}{3}}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\sqrt{\frac{580}{3}}}
\]
